properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): renaming a component whose MEANING changed (cmp:gateway → cmp:router, after the owner kept flo2's own gateway) took a delete, a re-create and re-drawn edges, and the node's history was lost. Ids are semantic slugs by convention and immutable keys by construction. Lineage is kept per item, keyed by id. No served tool moves an id. The one merge path (an asserted DUPLICATES and then a heal merge) cannot be steered: "the alphabet chose the victim", and it kept the OLD id
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-09-29, item I22 of art:dev-reflow2-two-agent-exercise-feedback-2026-09-29.

① OBSERVED (friction #7, 0.74.0): "Renaming a component = delete_node + add_component + re-draw edges (cmp:gateway → cmp:router after the owner kept flo2's gateway). Expected: a rename or id-move that keeps the edges and history. Cost: 1 delete, ~4 re-drawn edges, and the history of the old node lost." NOT affected: a change of `name` alone, which add_component revises in place under the same id.

② PRECEDENT: searched ("rename a node id", "restructuring ... keep its history") in both designs.
- cap:lineage-is-kept-per-item: each node carries its own content hash and the hash it replaced, keyed by id.
- dec:identity-out-of-band: ids are assigned without coordination.
- dec:idea-one-way-to-name-which-node-across-the-tool-surface: aliases on parameters, "No renames".
- cap:bl-180: restructuring is safe only when function is provably preserved; nothing computes it.
- No record of an id move.

③ CANDIDATES:
- (a) a rename tool exists and was missed;
- (b) keeping the id and revising the name was the right move, and the report's premise is wrong;
- (c) the merge machinery can act as a rename;
- (d) no route exists.

④⑤ MEASURED at 0.74.0:
- The served tool list (grep of the tool handlers) holds merge_designs, apply_merge, record_alias and move_component, and nothing that moves an id. record_alias says it "RENAMES NOTHING". move_component moves on the spine, not the key. So (a) is refuted.
- In an isolated scratch graph: cmp:gateway with PROVIDES/CONSUMES, a new cmp:router, and `DUPLICATES {basis: asserted}` gateway→router. propose_heal then proposes Merge keep_id=cmp:gateway, remove_id=cmp:router, with would_destroy saying: "THE ALPHABET CHOSE THE VICTIM: both carry the same provenance, so the smaller id survived (BL-29)". The merge keeps the OLD id, so (c) is refuted as a rename route.
- (b) is partly true: keeping cmp:gateway with name "Router" keeps edges and lineage. But the id then asserts a meaning the owner withdrew, in every edge echo, citation and search hit, and ids are taught as semantic slugs (`cmp:<slug>`).

⑥ CLASS: an identifier that is both a MEANING (the slug convention) and a KEY (immutable, lineage-bearing, cited in prose). When the meaning moves, one of the two must lie: either the id, or the history (by deletion). A fix at the class either separates the key from the slug, or offers a move that re-keys edges, carries lineage, and leaves the old id resolvable as an alias so prose citations do not dangle.

⑦⑧ OWED: a test that fails today (after a move, every edge, the lineage chain and a get_node on the old id all resolve to the new node), and the fix. The shape is open in dec:idea-a-node-can-be-re-keyed-and-keep-its-edges-lineage-and-old-name.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED:
- How many prose citations of an old id exist across reflow2's own design. Not measured.
- Whether the heal merge's survivor rule should instead take the NEWER node when the DUPLICATES edge is asserted in one direction. Not examined.
